relationship.condition: Access to practical training and information supported adoption of multistrata live fences; payments and assistance were substitutes rather than synergistic.
relationship.note: Adoption association for an enabling factor; not an NbS outcome effect or a quantitative operational score.

context.practice_as_described: Deliberately planted trees integrated with permanent cattle pastures, including multistrata live fences along pasture edges. Baseline for program comparisons: cattle farmers not participating in the Regional Integrated Silvopastoral Approaches to Ecosystem Management Project (RISEMP).
context.note: Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) is a financial incentive, not an ecosystem effect. Follow-up survey: 101 farmers, 66 program participants and 35 non-participants, December2008–February2009 (p5). Nominal random assignment may be biased by selection and acceptance (p4 footnote2); small technical-assistance-only subgroup (five respondents). Associations do not prove causal effects. Silvopastoral family supported by permanent pasture/cattle context and Table1p3: fences provide fodder/shade, not cropland, wind-shelter or contour-buffer intervention. No generalization to all agroforestry families. Income high follows current project CRI lookup; SRC still says upper_middle (metadata reconciliation pointer). Climate class omitted; humid subtropical source label not forced into vocabulary. Process: actual v1.9.4 source reread; changes replace unregistered staging only, no reviewer approval. Table5p8 multistrata technical assistance coefficient1.942, SE0.79, p<0.05; do not infer universal response for simple fences (p7 says technical assistance alone did not increase simple-fence adoption).
